Variants.Content: Harlaw is located in the eastern Iron Islands. It is one of the more populated and relatively fertile islands in the archipelago, across the sea towards the west coast of Westeros. House Harlaw and its many branches own castles and harbors on the island; the islanders also believe in the Drowned God, but rely more on farming, trade and long-term operations than many ironmen.
Entry Harlaw Local families also relied on salt fish, ore, barren fields, sheltered anchorages, and longships to return home; if any road, well, or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Harlaw They will also recognize the accents, laws and credentials of the Iron Islands; reputations may travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar or horse's hoof.

Entry Harlaw If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.
Entry Harlaw A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Harlaw They care about salt fish, ore, barren fields, sheltered anchorages, and the return of longships. They also look at whether seeds are left after collecting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
